Subject: SLA subscription bundling question & rapid-response credits

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the time last week. As we map out our 2027 POC and potential production rollouts, procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of your SLA packaging options and any add-on credits you offer for rapid incident response. Specifically: 

- Do you have a flat monthly retainer model for faster P1/P2 response (vs. per-incident pricing)?
- If we sign a 12-month commit, what discounts are typical across uptime tiers (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99)?
- Can you bundle dedicated capacity (GPU pods) with premium support and give an example TCO?
- Do unused rapid-response minutes/credits roll over or expire monthly?

We want something predictable for budgeting — mixing a commit with an ops retainer might be ideal if it keeps unit economics sensible. Can you send a short proposal or a price table we can ship to procurement?

Thanks,
Ravi Patel
Head of Platform Ops | Helix AI

Helix AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA subscription bundling question & rapid-response credits

Ravi — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise proposal and attached a pricing table (SLA_Pricing_Table_v3.xlsx) that shows the standard bundles and a couple of optional add-ons. High level: 

1) Core uptime tiers (monthly commitment pricing examples)
   • Standard (99.9%) — baseline support, 48h P3 triage, next-business-day P2.
   • Enhanced (99.95%) — 4h P2, 1h P1 response target, 24/7 on-call for severity 1, includes 60 rapid-response minutes / month.
   • Premium (99.99%) — 15min P1 target, 30min P2 target, 24/7 dedicated escalation lane, includes 200 rapid-response minutes / month and prioritized routing.

2) Rapid-response credit options
   • Hourly retainer (prepaid) — blocks of 500 / 1,000 minutes billed monthly; unused minutes roll over for 3 months.
   • Per-incident add-on — flat fee + per-minute rate for ad-hoc escalation.

3) Dedicated capacity bundle
   • We can attach a reserved GPU pool (configurable size) to an Enhanced or Premium SLA. Example: 2x reserved pods + Premium SLA — discount applies on committed spend. I included an example TCO in the attached xlsx.

4) Discounts and commit structure
   • 12-month commit: standard concession is 8–12% depending on committed spend band.
   • Volume-tiering: above $X/month we layer an additional 3–5% credit.

What I propose as a starting point for Helix: Premium SLA with a 12-month commit + 1,000 minute retainer (rollover 3 months) — we can show a 10% commit discount and include the first month of rapid-response minutes as a credit. That keeps your predictable unit cost while covering peak early-usage risk.

I also attached a short mutual action plan link that outlines steps to contract (https://redwood-drive.internal/SLAs/HLX-3921-MAP). If procurement wants a more formal offer, I can loop Karthik (sales) and Irene (ops) and draft a consolidated quote + MRAP.

Notes: the pricing table contains per-hour on-call rates, incident uplift fees, and a comparison of retention vs ad-hoc billing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk procurement through the tradeoffs.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Soojin — this is helpful, thanks. A few quick clarifications from procurement and engineering: 

- Procurement wants to see a banded discount schedule tied to committed spend (we'll likely be north of $250k ARR if we go Dedicated). Can you make the discount tiers explicit in numbers (not ranges)?
- On rollover: 3 months is reasonable; can you confirm if there is a cap on total rollover accumulation?
- Engineering asked if the Premium 15min P1 target is SLA-backed with credits (i.e., if you miss P1 target, what is the credit formula?).
- We'd like an example where we commit 24 months — is there an additional uplift for longer-term commits?

Procurement also wants the mutual action plan as a downloadable PDF for their packet. Can you produce that and include a draft statement of work (SOW) that lists expected onboarding milestones and ops contact handoff?

If you can get a firm quote by EOD tomorrow Pacific, procurement will review and try to return a redline quickly.

Ravi

Ravi — looping in operations and commercial to lock this down. TL;DR answers below and a firm offer we can put into a quote: 

• Commit discount (explicit tiers):
  – $0–$250k ARR: 6%
  – $250k–$750k ARR: 10%
  – $750k+ ARR: 14%

• 24-month uplift: additional 3% on top of the committed band (applies if same committed ARR is sustained for entire 24 months).

• Rollover cap: unused rapid-response minutes may roll over up to twice the monthly allotment (e.g., 200 min/month cap -> rollover max 400 min). After that cap, minutes expire.

• SLA credits: Premium tier (15min P1 target) is SLA-backed. Credit formula: for P1 incidents where response >15 minutes, customer receives a pro-rated credit equal to X% of monthly SLA fee per incident (see attached MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_HLX-3921.pdf for full table). We can make the credit multiplier more aggressive if you want a stronger penalty for repeated misses.

• Dedicated capacity + Premium bundle example (annualized): 2x reserved GPU pods + Premium SLA at $Y/month net after the 10% commit discount (we'll include line-item TCO with server, network egress estimate and per-token inference rate).

I'll prepare a formal quote and SOW today and attach the MAP and SOW as PDF for procurement. If that works, we can push a DocuSign link and aim to have an executed order within the week.

Next steps I recommend:
 1) I will upload a formal quote to HubSpot (deal HLX-3921) and send a DocuSign link.
 2) Irene will reach out to schedule the onboarding kickoff meeting and confirm ops SLAs and contact roster.
